title: Assured audit streaming to external observability (SIEM / webhooks / Splunk / Datadog)
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Context: Redwood generates high-fidelity audit events (authn/authz, config changes, admin actions, deployments). Customers in regulated industries demand reliable delivery into their observability stacks (SIEMs, Splunk HEC, Datadog, or customer-managed webhook collectors) with predictable guarantees and security controls. Current state: events are emitted to internal pipelines and retained for X days, and we have a basic webhook fanout implementation with best-effort retries. This ticket defines a hardened, observable, and configurable delivery subsystem for audit events to external endpoints.

Goals:
- Provide per-customer configurable sinks: webhook endpoints, Splunk HEC, Datadog HTTP API, syslog (via gateway).
- Delivery semantics: at-least-once with optional idempotency guarantees; documented dedupe window and guidance for exactly-once where possible.
- Strong delivery SLAs and delivery metrics surfaced to Console (success rate, median delivery latency, queue depth, DLQ rate).
- Backpressure and retry strategy with dead-lettering and configurable retention.
- Security: HMAC signing for webhook payloads, TLS enforcement, endpoint allowlist, and support for customer-managed auth (token rotations).
- Operational tooling: retry controls, replays for a timeframe, per-destination throttling and throttling escalation policies.

Non-goals:
- Full exactly-once semantics across arbitrary third-party endpoints (we will provide idempotency tokens and delivery guarantees within documented bounds but not distributed transaction guarantees).
- Building custom connectors for every SIEM vendor beyond generic HTTP/HEC/syslog patterns (we will add specific templates for Splunk and Datadog first).

Proposed design (summary):
1) Event envelope: audit events published to the internal durable stream (Kafka-backed / durable queue). Envelope includes event_id (UUID), created_at, tenant_id, event_type, payload, schema_version, idempotency_key, sequence_number (optional).
2) Delivery workers: stateless workers consume from the durable stream and write to a per-destination staging queue (durable). Each destination has a DeliveryConfig (endpoint, auth, retry_policy, rate_limit, batch_settings).
3) Guaranteed at-least-once: workers persist attempt metadata to a DeliveryState store (durable) before sending; on success mark delivered and remove. For idempotent destinations we attach idempotency_key in headers to allow dedupe.
4) Retries & backoff: exponential backoff with jitter, capped at configurable max_retries. After max_retries, event moves to customer-scoped DLQ for manual review / replay.
5) Batch vs single: support small batching for high-throughput endpoints (Splunk HEC bulk) with clear upper bounds on batch size and aggregated response handling.
6) Signing & integrity: webhooks signed with HMAC-SHA256 using per-destination key stored in KMS; fallback to mutual TLS for enterprise customers.
7) Rate-limiting & backpressure: per-tenant and per-endpoint token bucket enforcement. If external endpoint returns 429 or connection failures, we throttle and expand retry windows rather than dropping silently.
8) Observability & SLOs: surface metrics per destination: delivery_success_rate (1m/1h/24h), median_delivery_latency, queue_depth, dlq_count. Console will show health and allow replay.
9) Failure modes & guarantees: define SLA targets: 99.9% of events delivered to healthy endpoints within 5 minutes under steady load; guarantees apply only when endpoint responds with 2xx and TLS verified. Document limitations (e.g., customer endpoint misconfigurations, network partitions).

Acceptance criteria:
- Delivery subsystem can be configured per customer for Splunk HEC and Datadog endpoints and generic webhook.
- System demonstrates at-least-once behavior in integration test harness (simulated failures, network drops).
- Console shows delivery metrics and per-destination DLQ counts.
- Security: webhooks signed and verifyable; keys stored in KMS; token rotation tested.
- End-to-end demo: replaying a 24h DLQ into a Splunk HEC test instance via Console.

Implementation milestones:
- Spike: evaluate durable queue (Kafka vs managed pub/sub) and persistence model (done).
- API: DeliveryConfig CRUD + Console toggles (in progress).
- Worker: delivery worker with retries and DLQ (in progress).
- Integrations: Splunk HEC template, Datadog template, generic webhook (next).
- Observability: metrics + Console UI (blocked by backend metrics schema).

Security considerations:
- Ensure event payloads do not leak private keys; redact sensitive fields before external delivery unless customer opts into full event export.
- KMS-based signing keys with IAM controls; rotate keys without losing ability to validate recent events (we will embed key_id in signature header).
- Rate-limit secrets access from delivery workers and log only masked tokens.

Operational runbook (high-level):
- If a destination fails > threshold, escalate to on-call and notify tenant owner.
- Provide a Console permit to pause delivery to a destination and drain or replay after remediation.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Exactly-once: we will document constraints and provide idempotency helpers; full exactly-once across arbitrary endpoints is not feasible without customer cooperation.
- Retention bounds for DLQ / replay window. Proposed default: 30 days; configurable per-enterprise contract.
- Ingress throttling model for extremely chatty tenants: require Dedicated tier or rate-limited ingress.
comments: 2026-02-20 - Design kickoff: reviewed envelope schema and shoplifted HEC batch format; agreed on at-least-once with idempotency tokens. Attendees: Priya, Marco, Sanjay (SRE), Elena (Security).

2026-02-25 - Spike complete: validated Kafka consumer group pattern and durable per-destination staging queue. Performance sketch: 2000 eps per worker with batching. Spike notes in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/AUDIT/spike-delivery-kafka-results.
2026-03-02 - PR opened for DeliveryState persistence and worker skeleton: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/342. Initial integration tests added for Splunk HEC happy path.

2026-03-05 - Security review preliminary: Elena requested HMAC headers include key_id and timestamp to mitigate replay attacks. Also requested CI test for key rotation. Action: Marco to add rotation test.
2026-03-09 - Discovered issue: large payloads cause Splunk HEC 413 responses; added server-side enforced max_payload_size and batching guardrails. Temporary patch in PR #350.
2026-03-12 - Working on observability hooks: Prometheus metrics + Console API to surface per-destination delivery rate. Next: wire metrics to Console dashboard and add replay button.
